items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: But I got to play a lot actually, due to the efforts of Sal Nistico, who got me on the band. Sal used to say to Woody, you know, “Let him play.”

ctx.x: I didn’t ask you about — you had a year with Woody Herman?

No, hell no. How about like three and a half months or something like that. There’s two Brignolas. There’s Mike Brignola, who is with Woody Herman’s band now, happens to be the baritone player too. He has the record for being probably next to Frank Tiberi, the guy the most, the fellow that’s been with Woody Herman’s band the longest. He joined in 1979 and has been the baritone player since then. Coincidentally, we have the same name, and we play the same instrument. He’s about twenty years younger than I am. His…
